history.text: Beneath the plates the mantle turns over in two broad upwellings on opposite sides of the world, with cold sinking sheets between them; plumes rise from the upwellings' margins and stay fixed while the plates pass over them.

Old cores, swept together over the sinking mantle between the upwellings, collide and weld into the First Land; their seams become the inland belts of Gaffa, Khohalis and Demani and the old core under Garyk.

Lying long over the mantle like a lid, the First Land comes to sit above one of the upwellings, which domes it up and rifts it apart around Garyk; the rifts become passive, smooth coasts with wide shelves.
Gaffa, Khohalis and Demani break away from Garyk's side and drift together to the far side of the world, some twelve thousand kilometres, each turning about its own pole; Garyk stays behind.

Leading edges override sinking sea floor: coastal ranges, volcanoes and island arcs grow along them. The sea floor that still trails a sinking slab is pulled fast; Gaffa, Khohalis and Demani, whose slabs are gone and whose edges now ride over the sea floor ahead, have slowed to a few centimetres a year.

Plumes rising from the upwellings' margins build the open-sea archipelagos; each plate carries the older volcanoes away along its motion, where they sink into lines of seamounts, oldest farthest from the plume.
The Northern Garyk Sea Plate closes on Garyk; its northern ranges rise along the seam.
Wear and the slow rebound of the crust soften the old belts to rounded hills and lower the young ranges.
Caren is set down whole by the gods into the sea where the First Land had broken apart. It takes no part in the turning of the plates.

caren.summary: Caren is the Godstone: a single block laid down by the gods and their angels, not raised by the turning of the plates. It has no fault, no volcano and no rift, and it does not drift with the plate it rests on.

rocks.note: fine, even, almost without seams; it does not weather into tors
banded white and grey; the classic building stone
thin, fertile, with springs where it meets the granite

caren.earthquakes: none: the Godstone does not move; tremors from the sea floor around it are felt only faintly on its coasts

garyk.core: old core of granite and gneiss under the interior (part of the First Land)
